minutes.headline: School Committee held the FY15 budget hearing, heard the ALICE lockdown proposal, then went into executive session on bargaining.
minutes.summary: The superintendent presented the recommended FY15 school budget at the annual hearing, covering enrollment, school choice, special education drivers, staffing additions and ways to close the gap with the town manager's budget. The committee then approved minutes, a line item transfer for high school roof work, donations and a policy, and heard a presentation on the ALICE safety protocol. The meeting ended in executive session on collective bargaining.

what_happened.line: The superintendent presented the recommended FY15 school budget at the annual hearing, then the hearing was adjourned.
The superintendent said carryover and bus fees would be applied back toward the budget to close the gap with the town manager's budget.
The committee heard a presentation on the ALICE school safety protocol and set a parent informational meeting for April 30.
The committee voted to accept donations and to waive reading and approve a policy at third reading; the votes were not audible.
The committee entered executive session on collective bargaining by roll call; the outcome of the high school roof line item transfer was not audible.

why_it_matters: The gap between the school and town manager budgets decides how much of the school budget is funded, and how much is covered by one-time sources such as carryover and bus fees rather than the town budget, mostly taxes.
Tuition for out-of-district special education placements drives much of the non-personnel increase, so state circuit breaker reimbursement affects how much of that cost falls on local funds.
